newsitem.title: USA: Anheuser-Busch Q2 worldwide beer volume up 0.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Anheuser-Busch Q2 worldwide beer volume up 0.8 pct.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc said Wednesday its worldwide beer volume rose 0.8 percent to 25.6 milion barrels in the second quarter, compared with 25.4 million in the 1996 period.
Domestic volume was also up about 0.8 percent at 23.8 million barrels, while international volume rose 1.2 percent to 1.8 million barrels.
Anheuser-Busch said it achieved the 0.8 percent increase in domestic volume despite a difficult pricing environment in certain markets in 1997 compared to 1996.
The brewer said beer price discounting, initiated by its competitors, continued into the second quarter.

"Our policy is to match competitive discounting," August Busch III, chairman, said in a statement. "Although this may dampen short-term earnings growth, this strategy should enhance our market share position and maximize shareholder value over the long term."
Anheuser said its share of domestic beers shipments for the first six months of the year was 44.3 percent, essentially unchanged from a year ago.

Anheuser reported second quarter earnings of $0.76 per fully diluted share, up from $0.70 a year ago, from continuing operations. For the first six months of the year, it earned $1.27 a share, up from $1.17 a share excluding a gain.

Its six-month worldwide beer volume gained 1.3 percent to 47.4 million barrels. Domestic volume rose 0.6 percent to 44.2 million barrels and international volume gained 12.4 percent to 3.2 million barrels.

Anheuser said total international beer volume growth was led by significant volume expansion in the United Kingdom and China. Strong growth in China led to the expansion of the Wuhan brewery, which is expected to be complete in 1998, doubling the plant's capacity to 2.1 million barrels a year.

Anheuser said attendance at its theme parks was up six percent for the first six months of 1997 compared with the year-ago period. Increased attendance and higher in-park visitor spending led to increased profit contribution by Busch Entertainment Corp compared to a year ago.

Metal Container Corp, the can manufacturing unit, reported increased operating results for the first six months of 1997 compared with a year ago due to higher volume, continued productivity improvements and reduced distribution costs.
